pairs.subject: release-pipeline
pairs.evidence: features/data-releases/snapshot.ts:29 The public snapshot retains its schema version because added fields are considered additive, whereas the standard requires surveying readers or versioning additions when external readers cannot be surveyed.

techniques.evidence: features/data-releases/manifest.ts:225 The generator groups every supplied ingest run by date, including failed and running attempts; it does not implement the standard's commit-derived, audience-filtered changelog or unreleased ledger.

features/data-releases/getDataReleasesData.ts:216 Each download constructs its artifact from the current mutable store after reading manifest statistics; there is no pinned release snapshot or durable build-to-publish artifact handoff.

features/data-releases/snapshot.ts:37 The unchanged schema accompanies added nodeKinds/edgeRels fields, justified at lines 29–31 by additivity rather than demonstrated reader tolerance; repository searches located no external-reader survey.

features/data-releases/getDataReleasesData.ts:217 Download returns serialized bytes without requiring successful certification or a verification verdict keyed to those bytes; the existing certification concerns manifest metadata rather than the complete snapshot payload.

features/data-releases/snapshot.ts:202 Payload bytes are measured and displayed, but searches found no snapshot byte ceiling, committed size baseline, delta gate, or ratchet; row-count caps do not bound variable-size row properties.

features/data-releases/feedIndex.ts:73 These are content feeds and JSON data downloads; context and repository searches for updater/auto-update machinery found no installed-application update chain belonging to this context.

pairs.registryProposal: Clarify applicability to independently released datasets: identify the required change-history source and artifact verification equivalents when releases have ingest lineage and schema consumers rather than executable installers.
